defect.summary: THE READER IS NEVER TOLD WHICH ACT IT IS DECIDING, AND THE GLUE CANNOT HAND IT A HARM BASKET, A ROSTER OR THE BOOK'S PREDECESSORS (the Stop-1 note F-7, F-3; audit A-2, A-6). wire() passes readers no act identity, opens the witness's book only for a class basket, and never follows the book's declared retired predecessor.
defect.ground: Contract M3; audit 2026-10-15 18:40Z A-2 (the machine glue as its own ticket) and A-6 (the predecessor-chain latch). FIX: WireOptions gains gate2Harm (the reader's Gate2Harm), gate2RosterPath (the interest book; may equal gate1BookPath) gate2DecidingActionId (string or null) and gate2UnderivedWord (the frame's underived word, string or null, passed through to the reader). gate2Harm without gate2BookPath → NOT WIRED, GATE2_HARM_WITHOUT_BOOK (the chain is never read in harm mode); gate2Harm and gate2 together → WireUsageError. The book's first line gives bookBoundaryAt and retired {path, sha256}: each predecessor must sit in the book's own directory, exist as a regular file and hash to its declared sha256, and is opened as a chained log for the LATCH ONLY, recursively until retired: null; the first link that fails is handed to the reader as a stub that fails its readability gate (→ G2_PREDECESSOR_NOT_READABLE unless an ALARM stands). The roster is read from the interest book (records of the origin subjects with a subjectSeq and an actionId; unreadable → null → G2_ROSTER_NOT_READABLE). In harm mode the reader is handed a full-record view of the book (witnessed, hash, recordType), GATE2_BOOK_CEILING is not appended, and the census prints HARM <harmClass>, the latch state and the code. Everything else in wire() is byte-identical; wire() stays once-per-action. T32's coverage bound lives here too.
